title: Eternal Spirit! We Confess
description: Eternal Spirit! We Confess in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 133, headed “The operations of the Holy Spirit”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: E-ter-nal Spir-it! we con-fess And sing the won-ders of thy grace; Thy power con-veys our bless-ings down From God the Fa-ther and the Son.

lines: And sing the wonders of thy grace;
Thy power conveys our blessings down
From God the Father and the Son.
Our shades and darkness turn to day;
Thine inward teachings make us know
Our danger and our refuge too.
Thy power and glory works within,
And breaks the chains of reigning sin,
And forms our wretched hearts anew.
The troubled conscience knows thy voice,
Thy cheering words awake our joys;
Thy words allay the stormy wind,
And calm the surges of the mind.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
